source.description: Real, unmodified snapshot of Gunicorn's HTTP message parser at the pre-fix release 21.2.0. `set_body_reader` accepts conflicting/duplicate Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding headers leniently, enabling HTTP request smuggling and endpoint-restriction bypass (fixed in 22.0.0). A single vulnerable file is snapshotted (the faithful minimal slice), not the whole 9 MB repo.

notes: This is a deliberately HARD real-world case: request smuggling is a protocol-level flaw with no single obvious sink, so it stress-tests recall of the LLM lens / semgrep (which are not available in a bare CI env — this fixture's score is deferred to a live/tooled run). The citation anchors to the lenient Transfer-Encoding handling in set_body_reader. severity high; source_lens omitted (source-agnostic match).

findings.title: HTTP request smuggling via lenient Content-Length / Transfer-Encoding parsing
